clue.text: Stay to hear Terry who was held hostage

indicators.note: to hear says the surname is to be taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: Terry Waite, the Church of England envoy held hostage in Lebanon from 1987 to 1991

explanation.surface: An invitation to linger and listen to a famous former hostage tell his story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' marks a homophone: the surname of Terry Waite, the Anglican envoy held captive in Beirut, is said the same way as the word for stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay somewhere is to remain or linger, which is a close synonym.

clue.text: Independent politician travels here and there for rallies

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
to rove is to wander from place to place

explanation.surface: A lone non-party candidate tours the constituency holding rallies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rallies' looks like a noun for political meetings, but it is a verb: a patient rallies, gets better.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover or get better, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Sort of town Communist liberated

parts.note: a spa town, such as Bath or Harrogate, is built round mineral springs
Red is a familiar label for a communist

explanation.surface: A kind of town was freed by a Communist force.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spared is let off or released, much as one liberated is set free.

clue.text: Study period said to be right

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken, and their sound gives the entry

parts.note: to con is to study; a session is a period of time spent on something

explanation.surface: A spell of study is claimed to be the correct thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: CON (study) plus SESSION (period), spoken together, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A concession can be a right or privilege granted, such as a trading franchise.

clue.text: Enchanted — and about to get hurt

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
harmed means hurt, having come to harm

explanation.surface: Someone bewitched and about to suffer injury, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmed and enchanted both describe being under a spell or delighted.

clue.text: Plants needing some drastic action

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain plants need emergency treatment to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Plants needing' as the definition, but 'needing' is only a link word joining the definition 'Plants' to the wordplay 'some drastic action'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are succulent desert plants, so they are an example of plants.

clue.text: Rebellious minister is cad and is prejudiced

indicators.note: a rebellious group breaks ranks, so these letters break out of their order

explanation.surface: A disloyal government minister turns out to be a bounder and a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebellious' rearranges the letters of MINISTER IS CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate against people is to treat them unfairly out of prejudice.

clue.text: Preface for this writer written retrospectively

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so this word is put down backwards

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves gives me

explanation.surface: An author explains a foreword was added after the book was finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written retrospectively' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a short introduction or preamble to a book or speech.

clue.text: Marine creature mum has eaten — horrible!

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so these letters are put in a new, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Mother has swallowed some sea animal, and it is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges EATEN into NATEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manatee, or sea cow, is a large plant-eating mammal of warm coastal waters.

clue.text: Duck when escort gets hit

indicators.note: a word that gets hit is knocked about, so its letters are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone ducks when their companion is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets hit' rearranges ESCORT. 'Duck' looks like a verb, take cover, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoter is a dark-plumaged sea duck of northern waters.

clue.text: Article about group of people in the middle of Russia, Muslims

indicators.note: in says the whole assembly sits inside the letters taken from the country name
the middle of picks the two central letters of the country name
about means surrounding, so the article goes round the next piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a race is a group of people of common descent

explanation.surface: A report on a community living in central Russia who are Muslim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the article round the group, and 'in' sets that inside the two central letters of Russia. 'Muslims' is the medieval Christian sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracens was the medieval European name for Arab or Muslim peoples, especially at the time of the Crusades.

clue.text: Detected journalist's halo maybe!

definitions.meaning: a halo is a disc floating over the head of an editor, Ed

explanation.surface: A reporter's saintly glow has been spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a halo is a DISC, and it sits OVER the head of ED, the usual crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detected has been found out or noticed, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Ladies keep a tally of letters, we hear

parts.note: to count is to keep a tally

indicators.note: we hear says the letters are to be written as they are pronounced

parts.note: letters here are two of the nineteenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Women who keep a record of correspondence, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter S is spoken and spelt 'ess', so the letters S S, said aloud, give ESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Countesses are noblewomen, wives of earls or counts, and so titled ladies.

clue.text: Place of bitterness not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping means the next item is dropped from the word

parts.note: spite is malicious bitterness
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A spot where resentment refuses to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not keeping' drops P from SPITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or plot, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Flexing muscle, sire is carrying one powerful weapon

indicators.note: carrying means holding the next piece inside
flexing bends and twists, so these letters are bent into another order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A father flexes his muscles and turns out to be armed to the teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flexing' rearranges MUSCLE SIRE IS, and 'carrying' puts I (one) inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise missile is a low-flying guided missile, a long-range weapon.

clue.text: Underground workers not given right dogs

indicators.note: not given means this letter is held back from the word

parts.note: colliers are coal miners

explanation.surface: Miners who were refused their due rights, or perhaps their dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not given' drops R from COLLIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Collies are a breed of sheepdog, so they are an example of dogs.

clue.text: Designer, the female artist leading French fashion

indicators.note: leading means going in front of the next piece

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
RA, a Royal Academician
ton is a French word for fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A female artist at the forefront of Paris fashion makes a name as a designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an English furniture designer of the late eighteenth century.

clue.text: Fool cuts material short

indicators.note: short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: cloth is material, fabric

explanation.surface: An idiot snips a piece of fabric too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the final H from CLOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for an idiot.

clue.text: William Brown's friend mad for biscuits

parts.note: Ginger is a member of William Brown's gang, the Outlaws, in Richmal Crompton's Just William books
nuts means mad

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's pal is crazy about biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: William Brown is the unruly schoolboy hero of the British Just William children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger nuts are hard, ginger-flavoured biscuits popular in Britain for dunking.

clue.text: Author sounding fresh

indicators.note: sounding says the word is spoken, giving the novelist's surname

parts.note: green means fresh or new

explanation.surface: A writer whose voice comes across as new.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist, author of Brighton Rock.

clue.text: Mount or hill in which sailor is buried

indicators.note: is buried means the sailor lies within the hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
AB, able seaman

explanation.surface: A mountain or hill where a seaman lies in his grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is buried' puts the sailor inside the hill; 'Mount' is a proper name here, the biblical hill in Galilee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Tabor is a hill in Galilee, site of the Transfiguration by tradition.

clue.text: Unmarried female writer having time wasted

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A single woman author whose hours went to waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent describes time or money squandered foolishly.

clue.text: Notice old politicians making off-the-cuff comments

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
Libs, Liberals, of the old Liberal Party that became the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: Former politicians are spotted speaking without notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb but is a noun, an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libs are improvised remarks, spoken without preparation.

clue.text: Biography, story about France's leader

indicators.note: about means going round the next piece

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A biography that tells the story of a French president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts F, the leader of France, inside LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A life is an account of someone's life story, a biography.

clue.text: Superficial brightness of hospital noticed on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says this word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: seen means noticed
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital whose shine is noticed only from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' puts SEEN around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheen is a soft lustre on a surface.

clue.text: Son gets box — one greedy for chocolates, maybe?

parts.note: a coffer is a strong box or chest

explanation.surface: A boy receives a box of chocolates and gobbles the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, flagged by 'maybe': chocolates are one thing a greedy eater might wolf down.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat greedily, so a scoffer gobbles food such as chocolates.
